title: Complete Identification of Macro Effects in Cyclic Cluster Graphs via Strongly Connected Hedges

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an SCC-condensation identification package, saturation and hedge-lift arguments, and a finite negative audit showing that a graphical SC-hedge is not generally a semantic nonidentification certificate on the frozen fixed-alphabet class. The surviving positive result was capped at subfield, below the field floor, while the load-bearing original-query hedge lemma still relied on undeclared ordinary-ID recursion; no in-scope repair could raise the novelty tier.
tldr: Absence of a query-relevant SC-hedge is sufficient for one observational formula for the macro effect, uniformly over the fixed finite full-support class \(\mathfrak M(G)\), even when compatible refinements contain nonlinear feedback and latent confounding. MacroSC-ID obtains the formula by preserving outcome-relevant strongly connected components, compiling each refinement into an acyclic tuple-valued block model, saturating only outcome-irrelevant split remnants, and running ordinary acyclic ID on the condensation. It terminates with either that uniform formula or an explicitly checkable graphical SC-hedge. This is a one-sided sufficiency result and a formula-or-graphical-obstruction compiler, not an if-and-only-if semantic criterion: for the frozen fixed-alphabet class, an SC-hedge is not in general a semantic nonidentification certificate.
gap: Ferreira--Assaad prove that an SC-hedge obstructs macro identification and explicitly state that completeness is open. Generalized cyclic ID is sound but expressly not known complete, and observational acyclification alone does not preserve the whole-block interventions required here.
fill: Prove the split-SCC obstruction, pointwise block representation, intervention-saturation invariance, tuple-ID soundness, original-query terminal certificate, and constructive hedge lift; integrate them into a deterministic formula-or-SC-hedge compiler. Audit rather than assume the published negative theorem's fit to fixed alphabets.
